S23.01.note: The gallery has its own inline create form (ProjectGallery.tsx around lines 180-300) as well as CreateProjectDialog; the gallery's Create button label was not confirmed in the source read.
steps: Click Projects in the left sidebar.
Click New project.
Type a name in the Project name box. Leave it empty first and check that submitting does nothing.
Click Create project (or press Enter in the name box).
Check that the new project opens as its own page with that name shown.
S23.01.where: Sidebar > Projects > New project > Project name > Create project

S23.02.note: The name and description edit fields and the Save button label in ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx were not confirmed in this read; the 'Project options' control is an aria-label only, not visible text.
steps: At creation, type a name and a Description, then click Create project.
Open the project, click the Project options button (top right of the project page).
Click Project settings and change the name or description.
Save, reload the page, and check the new name and description are still shown.
S23.02.where: Projects > New project > Description (at creation); later Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings

S23.03.note: The icon and colour controls have only aria-labels (for example 'Change project icon and colour' in apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx), not visible words, so the tester must find them by the icon; the picker and colour control are in ProjectGallery.tsx around lines 280-360.
steps: Click New project and click the icon button next to the Project name box to open the icon list.
Pick an icon, then pick a colour swatch.
Click Create project.
Look at the project card in the Projects list and at the project page header; both should show the chosen icon and colour.
S23.03.where: Projects > New project > icon button beside the name; later open a project and use its icon and colour control

S23.05.note: The page has tabs Chats, Artifacts, Work, Sources and Scheduled; there is no visible 'Instructions' tab (instructions sit under Project settings > Instructions) and no visible counts were found in the read, so the Expected wording differs.
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar, then click a project card.
Look at the page title and the description under it.
Look at the tabs: Chats, Artifacts, Work, Sources, Scheduled.
Compare with Expected: name, description, counts and the main sections.

S23.06.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that can generate
S23.06.note: The new-chat box uses a template placeholder 'New chat in ${project.name}' (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx line 1088); generation may be gated by plan.
steps: Open a project and stay on the Chats tab.
Check the list of conversations; click one to open it.
Type in the box that says 'New chat in <project name>' and send a message.
Go back to the project's Chats tab and check the new chat is listed.
S23.06.where: Projects > open a project > Chats tab

S23.07.needs: a paid account with project knowledge storage (a Free account is blocked) and a file to upload
S23.07.note: Upload button label was not found in the panel read; SourcesPanel.tsx shows 'Preview <file>' and 'Remove <file>' aria-labels. Earlier run recorded a plan gate on upload.
steps: Open a project and click the Sources tab.
Find the upload control in the Sources panel and choose a small text file.
Check the file appears in the list with a Preview button and a Remove button.
Preview and then remove it, and check the list updates.
S23.07.where: Projects > open a project > Sources tab

S23.08.needs: a paid account; for Google Drive the owner must set the Picker keys
S23.08.note: Marked unfinished in the audit: the Google Picker needs GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY and GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID, which are not set; text sources and add-source labels were not found in the read, and the Drive refresh control is aria-labelled 'Refresh <file> from Google Drive' (SourcesPanel.tsx line 757).
steps: Open a project and click the Sources tab.
Look for the add-source options (files, text, Google Drive).
Try adding a Google Drive file if the picker is shown.
Check the added source appears in the Sources list.
S23.08.where: Projects > open a project > Sources tab

S23.09.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that can generate
S23.09.note: Effect on chat answers is server-side (apps/web/lib/services/project-context-service.ts) and cannot be seen directly in the UI.
steps: Open a project, click Project options, then Project settings.
Type text in the Instructions box and save.
Reload, reopen Project settings and check the text is kept.
Start a new chat in this project, ask a question the instruction would change, and compare the answer.
S23.09.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Instructions

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

S23.11.note: Earlier run recorded Save staying disabled in settings; reload persistence was not confirmed.
steps: Open Project settings and find the Memory section.
Tick or untick 'Use memories from outside this project'.
Save, reload and reopen Project settings.
Check the box state and the explanation text under it are kept.
S23.11.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Memory

S23.12.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that can make an artifact
S23.12.note: Empty-state wording of ProjectArtifactsPanel.tsx was not read.
steps: Open a project and click the Artifacts tab.
Check the list of artifacts, or the empty state if none.
Create an artifact in a chat in this project, then return to the Artifacts tab.
Click the artifact and check it opens.
S23.12.where: Projects > open a project > Artifacts tab

S23.14.needs: a paid plan that allows Work
S23.14.note: The empty-state text is 'Switch a chat in {projectName} to Work and its runs will be listed here.' (ProjectWorkPanel.tsx line 119). How to switch a chat to Work was not confirmed.
steps: Open a project and click the Work tab.
Read the empty-state text.
Switch a chat in the project to Work and run a task.
Return to the Work tab and check the run is listed with its state.
S23.14.where: Projects > open a project > Work tab

S23.15.needs: a paid plan (Basic or higher); earlier run was blocked by the plan gate
S23.15.note: The create button label on the Scheduled tab was not confirmed; the schedule list lives in apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.tsx.
steps: Open a project and click the Scheduled tab.
Click the control that creates a routine or scheduled task.
Fill it in and save.
Check the new routine is listed on the project's Scheduled tab.
S23.15.where: Projects > open a project > Scheduled tab

S23.16.needs: a signed-in account; the chosen model must be allowed on the plan
S23.16.note: The new-chat default is applied in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx (no visible label).
steps: Open Project settings.
Find the Default model field and choose a model.
Save, then start a new chat inside the project.
Check the new chat's model selector shows the chosen default.
S23.16.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Default model

S23.20.needs: at least two projects with different names and descriptions
S23.20.note: Whether the search matches descriptions was not confirmed (ProjectGallery.tsx line 118 filter not fully read).
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar.
Click the search box with the placeholder 'Search projects...'.
Type part of a project's name, then part of its description.
Check that only matching projects stay in the list.
S23.20.where: Projects (sidebar) > search box at the top of the Projects page

S23.21.needs: a team workspace and a second account in it
S23.21.note: The share dialog says 'Only you can open this project. Switch to a team workspace to share it.' outside a team workspace (ProjectShareDialog.tsx line 79).
steps: Open a project in a team workspace and click Project options, then Share.
Read the dialog title 'Share <project name>' and the list of people.
Check the owner is shown with the detail 'Owner'.
Sign in as a second member and open the same project; check it appears as shared with you.
S23.21.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Share

S23.22.needs: two accounts in the same workspace with different roles
S23.22.note: The server-side enforcement is in apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts; the access labels are shown in the UI.
steps: Open Share for a shared project as the owner.
Change a member's access between Can view, Can edit and No access.
As that member, try to edit the project's instructions and try to view it.
Check the owner and member see what the role allows and that the server refuses edits from a view-only member.
S23.22.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Share > access dropdown next to a member

S23.23.needs: an owner or manager account and a second member account
S23.23.note: A separate 'Remove' control was not found; removal is shown as 'No access' in the code (ProjectSharingControls.tsx line 43).
steps: Open Share as the owner or a manager.
Click Add people and pick a workspace member.
Check the person appears in the list with a role.
Set that person to No access to remove them from the project, then check they lose it.
S23.23.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Share > Add people

S23.24.needs: a team workspace and a second account in it
S23.24.note: Copy link is also reachable from the card's Share action (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ProjectCard.tsx line 248).
steps: Open a shared project as the owner and click Project options, then Share.
Click Copy link.
Open the copied link in a private window signed in as a shared member.
Check the project opens for that member.
S23.24.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Share > Copy link

S23.29.needs: a project owner; file copy needs a plan with project knowledge storage
S23.29.note: A source comment in ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx (around line 436) says the duplicate route shipped without a caller; the button exists in code. Files duplicated wording is shown after duplication (line 155).
steps: Open Project settings as the project owner.
Click Duplicate.
Wait until the button stops showing 'Duplicating…'.
Check the copy appears in the Projects list with the same instructions and settings, and that its files are copied too.
S23.29.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Duplicate

S23.30.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S23.30.note: The archived-toggle label is a template 'Archived (${archivedProjects.length})'; that its contents are intact after restore was not confirmed.
steps: On the Projects page, open a project card's menu and click Archive.
Check the project leaves the active list.
Click the toggle that shows 'Archived (<n>)' and find the project.
Click Unarchive and check the project is back in the active list with its chats and files still there.
S23.30.where: Projects > card menu (More) > Archive; then Show archived toggle > Unarchive

S23.32.needs: a project owner and a test project
S23.32.note: The settings dialog text for non-Health projects was not read; the shown delete warning says chats are permanently deleted only for Health spaces (ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx line 230), so check the non-Health wording before testing.
steps: On the Projects page, open a project card's menu and click Delete.
Read the confirmation 'Delete "<name>"?' and click Delete to confirm.
Check the project is gone from the Projects list.
Open an existing chat that was in the project and check it still exists and is no longer filed under the project.
S23.32.where: Projects > card menu (More) > Delete > confirm Delete; or Project options > Project settings > Delete project?

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project
Use your profile and instructions for AGI

S23.33.needs: a signed-in account with some account-wide memories and chats
S23.33.note: The code excludes account-wide memory and profile instructions only; it does not show other chats being excluded, so the Expected wording goes beyond it. Generation was blocked in the earlier run.
steps: Open Project settings.
Untick 'Use memories from outside this project' and untick 'Use your profile and instructions for AGI'.
Save and reopen Project settings.
Ask a project chat a question about a memory or chat from outside the project, and check the answer does not use it.
S23.33.where: Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Memory and Personalization

S23.34.needs: a second account and a project shared with it
S23.34.note: The explanation text is 'This project’s instructions and files are shared with you. Your chats and memories here stay private to you.' (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx around line 1036); it only shows for shared projects.
steps: Sign in as a member of a team workspace and open a project shared with you.
Look for the label 'Shared with you' next to the title.
Read the line under the title: instructions and files are shared, your chats and memories stay private.
Compare with Expected; then open the owner's view and check the explanation is not shown there.
S23.34.where: Projects > open a project shared with you (you are a member) > read the line under the title
